title: Stopped on the wick
prompt: It is 09:50 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: A well-made trade can still be stopped. Look at where the stop belongs and why.

whyNot.label: a stop 50 points deeper
whyNot.why: It would have survived this, and it would have been placed for the outcome, not for the idea. The stop belongs just beyond the level that proves the setup wrong. Widening it to avoid a wick halves the R:R on every trade that works.

reference.summary: A textbook long with a stop just beyond the sweep low. A fast wick takes that stop and reverses to the previous day high. The setup, the stop and the target were right; the stop-out is the cost of a tight, correct invalidation. A wider stop would have survived and scored lower.

bias.why: Higher highs and higher lows on the Daily and 4H; the dip was a pullback.

decision.why: Everything required is present. Take it, or wait for the retrace.

take.why: Valid. This one gets stopped on a wick.

next_objective.why: Price was drawn to the previous day high (20,077.25). The question is where price was likely to be pulled, not what the next candle would do. A previous-day extreme is also a pool of buy-side or sell-side liquidity, so that answer is right on the side, if less exact.

annotations.label: Overnight low 19,918
annotations.why: Sell-side liquidity swept at the open.

annotations.label: Sweep low 19,901.5
annotations.why: The invalidation. A trade through it is a stop-out, wick or not.
annotations.decisionNote: Place the stop here. Not further 'in case'.

confluences.label: "A stop beyond a possible wick"
confluences.why: A stop placed for a wick you can't see isn't a stop for the idea.

trade.confirmationLabel: the displacement that closed above the last 5m high

lookFor: A stop-out followed by the move you wanted hurts, and isn't a mistake in the process.
Compare a stop beyond the invalidation with one placed for the outcome: the first costs a wick sometimes; the second costs R:R every time.
